title: SLO-driven traffic shaping and quota matrix
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures an operational design for a SLO-driven tenant traffic shaping layer and a compact quota matrix to enforce customer tiering, contractual SLAs, and noisy-neighbor controls across multi-region clusters. It is intended as a working draft for platform engineering and SRE to iterate on before we codify into the control plane and routing service.

Context and goals:
- Customers are on differentiated tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Enterprise) with explicit latency SLOs, throughput guarantees, burst entitlements, and billing commitments.
- We need deterministic behaviour when capacity is constrained: predictable degradation, preferential treatment by contract, and automated fallback to cheaper model variants or regions.
- The control plane must be able to express policy concisely and push enforcement signals to the edge router and serving runtime.
- Detect and mitigate noisy neighbors quickly without manual intervention.

High-level approach:
1) SLO-driven weights: each tenant gets a dynamic weight vector derived from their SLA profile, current SLO compliance signal (p95/p99), and recent spend. Weight components:
   - baseline_weight (from contract)
   - compliance_bonus (if historical SLOs met over window)
   - penalty_factor (if recent errors/latency spikes)
   The router computes an effective priority score = baseline_weight * (1 + compliance_bonus - penalty_factor). Scores normalize to allocate capacity share.

2) Quota matrix (compact canonical form):
   Columns: {tier, qps_limit, burst_tokens, window_seconds, reserved_capacity_pct, max_concurrent, downgrade_policy}
   Example rows (illustrative):
   - Gold: qps_limit=1200, burst_tokens=2400, window_seconds=60, reserved_capacity_pct=25, max_concurrent=200, downgrade_policy=regional-failover
   - Silver: qps_limit=300, burst_tokens=600, window_seconds=60, reserved_capacity_pct=10, max_concurrent=50, downgrade_policy=model-quantized-fallback
   - Bronze: qps_limit=60, burst_tokens=120, window_seconds=60, reserved_capacity_pct=0, max_concurrent=10, downgrade_policy=best-effort-queue
   - Enterprise: qps_limit=custom, burst_tokens=custom, reserved_capacity_pct=40, max_concurrent=500, downgrade_policy=priority-preempt

   Notes: burst_tokens are implemented with a token-bucket per-tenant and a separate global bucket to prevent cluster-level bursts from starving others. Reserved_capacity_pct reserves N% of pool for the tier even during contention.

3) Multi-region routing preferences:
   - Preferred region pinned by contract -> router uses local pool if available.
   - If preferred region SLO is at risk (p95 > threshold or queue depth>threshold), control plane flips a regional_fallback flag for that tenant to allow cross-region routing to healthy pools.
   - Cross-region routing must be cost-aware: we attach a cost-margin to remote pools (latency + egress) so the score favors local unless local degrades beyond threshold.

4) Noisy-neighbor detection and short-circuit mitigations:
   - Signals: sustained per-tenant p99 increase, sudden queue depth spike, disproportionate KV cache miss rate, abnormal GPU utilization per-tenant.
   - Fast mitigation flow (automated):
     a) Throttle burst allowance and reduce weight by penalty_factor increment.
     b) Limit max_concurrent to a safe floor and enable request-shedding for non-critical routes (embeddings, large-batch generates).
     c) If still violating after short cooldown, move tenant to isolated queue or gated dedicated pool (if reserved capacity configured) and open a ticket to SE.

5) Degradation and graceful fallback rules:
   - Per-route policy table: each route declares fallback_order = [same-model-quantized, smaller-model, cross-region-same-model, 503-with-retry-after]. Router consults tenant downgrade_policy then route fallback_order to choose action.
   - For Enterprise customers with reserved_capacity_pct, we prefer preemption of lower-tier bursts (not lowering reserved blocks) rather than immediate failover.

6) Control plane responsibilities:
   - Authoritative tenant SLA profiles (baseline_weight, quotas, reserved_capacity).
   - Real-time compliance engine: computes compliance_bonus and penalty_factor windows and emits delta to router every 10s.
   - Quota and token-bucket state storage (sharded, eventually-consistent) with short TTLs and periodic reconciliation.
   - Audit log generation for any preemption, downgrade, or cross-region routing decision for billing and compliance.

Implementation sketches and config snippets (pseudo-config):
   tenant_profiles: |
     tenant_id: rho-123
     tier: silver
     baseline_weight: 1.0
     reserved_capacity_pct: 10
     max_concurrent: 50
     downgrade_policy: model-quantized-fallback

   router_policy: |
     compute_effective_score(tenant) = normalize(baseline_weight * (1 + compliance_bonus - penalty_factor) - region_cost_margin)

Operational metrics to track (per-tenant and per-pool):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (model-level and route-level)
- qps, concurrent_requests, queue_depth
- token_bucket_tokens_remaining, burst_consumption_rate
- number_of_downgrades, cross_region_reroutes, preemptions
- eviction_count, time_to_recover_after_mitigation

Alerting and SLO definitions (examples):
- Critical alert: tenant_p99 > SLA_p99 + 20% for 2 consecutive minutes -> auto-penalty + paging to on-call
- Warning: tenant_queue_depth > 75% of max_concurrent for 1 minute -> reduce bursts; if persists escalate

Open design questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should penalty_factor be? We want fast mitigation but avoid oscillation. Suggested starting point: penalty ramp linear over 60s up to 0.5 weight reduction, decay over 5m.
- Global vs per-pool token buckets: global bucket limits cluster-level burst; per-pool buckets help local fairness. Both needed but parameters require tuning.
- Billing signals for cross-region fallback: do we bill cross-region egress to tenant or absorb as operational cost?
- On-prem/private deployments: reserved_capacity_pct semantics change if customer manages their own pool; need a simplified enforcement mode.

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Implement compliance_bonus/penalty_factor prototype in compliance-engine (INF-4821) -> owner: Marco
- [ ] Add quota matrix to router config schema and wire token-bucket enforcement -> owner: Asha
- [ ] Run chaos test that simulates noisy neighbor (CPU/GPU spike) and validate mitigation chain end-to-end -> owner: SRE
- [ ] Populate SLO catalog for tier mapping and publish to Confluence -> owner: Tina

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive in parts to speed iteration; if you prefer more conservative starting parameters call them out in PR.
- I want feedback on the downgrade_policy taxonomy (is it expressive enough for model-tiering and non-model routes?).

Appendix: quick glossary of terms used here:
- baseline_weight: contractual capacity share before runtime adjustments
- compliance_bonus: positive adjustment for reliable historical behavior
- penalty_factor: negative adjustment when SLOs degrade
- reserved_capacity_pct: percent of pool capacity held aside for a tier to guarantee minimal throughput during contention

End of draft.
